title: Dimethyltryptamine and the Recursive Reorganization of Consciousness
source_native_claims: Develops a multilevel causal architecture for how DMT reorganizes conscious experience across a compressed timescale, integrating pharmacokinetics, receptor signaling, cellular gain modulation, whole-brain dynamics, embodied physiology, phenomenology, memory, environment, repeated exposure, recovery, and post-session updating.

Presented as a Tier-2 special-case domain synthesis within the GCD–UMCP corpus; its central formal contribution is a prospective dual-reference architecture distinguishing departure from waking organization from approach toward a candidate recurrent DMT-state organization.

The proposed architecture is procedurally specified but empirically unvalidated; its scientific value depends on prospective testing, comparison with simpler models, preservation of negative results, and explicit contraction where its local predictions fail.
Offers no preparation, dosing, administration, or legal-circumvention guidance.
